items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Roe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Chonnonton peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.
Councillor Roe added additional reflections on the Wampum belts, and invited residents to continue their education on truth and reconciliation.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Roe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Hanmer directed a question to Mark Dykstra regarding the Fireworks By-law, and the different initiatives the City has taken to reduce the instances of fireworks in the City, including what the City is considering or might be considering going forward regarding fireworks. She was also curious about a coordinated approach to communication strategies regarding fireworks.

Mark Dykstra responded that it’s a cross-section divisional support effort, and that the team has been doing research to see what municipalities across the country are doing, to look at more stringent considerations around regulation. He mentioned that staff could work with other municipalities if directed by Council, and that they have been working with Communications on a strategy surrounding public safety and how best to share that.

Mayor McCabe spoke about the 2025 University Ave E project site and that the deadline for submissions has passed. There were a number of applications, and the project is possible due to the Federal Government’s Housing Accelerator Fund. She asked staff what the next steps are because of the significance of the project.
Ron Ormson responded with an update on the projects happening due to the Housing Accelerator Fund grant, including the Official Plan Review and 2025 University Ave E.
There are technical evaluations of the submissions that have to take place, and staff will look at compliance with the City’s goals. After which they will report back to Council.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Vasic wanted to highlight two events. Textile Magazine held their first event:

Black Talk. It was a conversation between the authors Hanif Abdurraqib and Antonio Michael Downing, and offered insight on the public record of Black Culture and Black Communities. The MC of the event really thanked City and Waterloo Public Library staff for the funding and also for working together with Textile, and how open, curious and responsive staff were to activism and advocacy. She wanted to highlight that the City should be proud of how well they worked together.

Councillor Vasic also mentioned the Planning Department and had a small story of good customer service, despite how busy they are. The Planner Aminu Bello gave her a heads up that there was an Informal Public Meeting coming up for something in her ward, and gave her an opportunity to review it and ask questions in advance. She offered her thanks to Planning for working so well with Council.

Councillor Wright wanted to acknowledge that Council did not sit last Monday, September 30 for the National Day of Truth and Reconciliation. Many Indigenous-led organizations across the community engaged with settlers to continue their education and encourage commitment to action towards reconciliation. She attended the Sunrise Ceremony at the University of Waterloo, and the opportunities to gather and commit to action are so important.

Mayor McCabe spoke about the Giraffe Parade in Waterloo Park this past Saturday, October 5 in tribute of Dr. Anne Innis Dagg, the renowned zoologist who was local to Waterloo and worked at the University. The event was helped by City staff through Community Services and the Community Grant Committee. Dr. Anne Innis Dagg wrote 60 journals on giraffes as well as a book on feminism in academia. TheMuseum in downtown Kitchener has an exhibit called, “Giraffe: A Heightened Experience” that is in honour of her and her research.

Councillor Roe mentioned that Saturday, October 5 was also the Ride for Refuge, which is a ride in solidarity with those seeking hope, safety, and freedom when fleeing conflict and persecution in other parts of the world. United College at the University of Waterloo partnered with Reception House for a ride in Waterloo, and Compass Refugee Centre had a ride at Doon Golf Club. Both were successful. Reception House brought 50 newcomers to the event, which was encouraging to see in a welcoming and supportive environment.
Councillor Roach wanted to congratulate Waterloo local Steven Lorentz for signing with the Toronto Maple Leafs.
